title: Claude identifies a CRISPR-like enzyme system in phages
summary: Anthropic says Claude agents found an uncharacterized reverse-transcriptase system after screening 200,000 proteins and guiding lab validation.
body:
## What happened
Anthropic said its new life-sciences group used Claude agents to identify a previously uncharacterized enzyme system in bacteriophages. The system, called array-associated reverse transcriptases (ARTs), combines a reverse-transcriptase gene, a neighboring accessory gene and a long array of repeating DNA sequences.

The finding emerged from a 21-hour search involving roughly 950 agents and 210 million tokens. Claude agents surveyed more than 200,000 reverse transcriptases, selected 3,500 unusual candidate systems and narrowed them to 20 for closer analysis. One agent noticed a repeat pattern beside an unusual reverse transcriptase that had not previously been recognized as part of a functional system.

Anthropic’s scientists then performed laboratory tests. Early results indicate that the repeat array is transcribed into multiple short RNAs, a feature that gives the system a superficial resemblance to programmable CRISPR biology. The company does not yet know what ART does, and its possible usefulness as a biotechnology tool remains unproven.

## Why it matters
The important claim is not that Claude has already created a new gene-editing platform. It is that a model-led workflow moved from large-scale sequence mining to a testable biological hypothesis, while human researchers retained responsibility for experiments. Anthropic says the lab works at BSL-1 and BSL-2 levels and does not handle human pathogens.

If ART’s function is confirmed, the episode could become an early example of AI helping scientists find overlooked molecular systems rather than merely summarizing published knowledge. For now, the discovery is best treated as a credible lead: the mechanism, programmability and practical value still await independent characterization.
title_zh: Claude在噬菌体中发现类CRISPR酶系统
summary_zh: Anthropic称，Claude智能体从20万个逆转录酶中筛出候选系统，并通过实验确认其具有此前未被注释的结构特征。
body_zh:
## 发生了什么
Anthropic表示，其新成立的生命科学团队利用Claude智能体，在噬菌体中识别出一种此前未被表征的酶系统。该系统被命名为“阵列关联逆转录酶”（ART），由逆转录酶基因、相邻的辅助基因，以及一长串重复DNA序列组成。

这项发现来自一次持续约21小时的搜索，期间约950个智能体消耗了2.1亿个词元。Claude先后检查了20万个以上的逆转录酶，筛出3500个异常候选系统，再缩小到20个重点对象。其中一个智能体注意到，某种非典型逆转录酶旁边存在此前未被识别的重复序列阵列。

随后，Anthropic研究人员进行了实验验证。初步结果显示，这组重复序列会被转录成多条短RNA，因此在形态上与可编程的CRISPR系统有相似之处。不过，ART究竟执行什么功能仍未确定，它能否成为生物技术工具也远未得到证明。

## 为什么重要
这条消息的价值不在于Claude已经制造出新的基因编辑平台，而在于它展示了一条由模型主导、最终落到实验验证的生物学发现流程。Anthropic强调，实验室目前只开展BSL-1和BSL-2级别工作，不处理能够感染人类的病原体。

如果后续研究确认ART的功能，这可能成为AI帮助科学家发现被忽略分子系统的早期案例，而不只是整理已有文献。现阶段更稳妥的判断是：这是可信的研究线索，但其作用机制、可编程性和实际价值仍等待独立验证。

sources.title: Claude discovers a novel enzyme system with CRISPR-like repeats
Anthropic says its biology lab has already found something big

featured_reason: It is the edition’s strongest evidence that AI agents can generate and experimentally advance genuinely new biological hypotheses.
featured_reason_zh: 它是本期最有分量的证据，显示AI智能体已能从海量生物数据推进可实验验证的新假设。
cat_take_zh: ART尚未证明能编辑基因，但950个智能体找到了值得实验室追踪的异常。
cat_take_en: ART is not yet a gene-editing tool, but 950 agents found an anomaly worth putting under laboratory scrutiny.
